transcript.text: someone hit my car at work this morning

Hi, I'm Sam, Wattle Car Insurance's AI claims assistant. You can talk to a person at any time. Just ask.

I'm sorry to hear about the accident. I can help you get a claim started.

First, is anyone hurt or in danger right now?
Hi Sam. Yeah, nobody's hurt, thank God. I'm fine. It's just my car, and it's drivable.

I'm glad no one was hurt. Before we go any further, I need to check who you are.

Could you please give me your policy number? If you don't have it handy, your date of birth and mobile number will work too.
WTL456790. It's Tom Nguyen.

Thanks, Tom, you're verified. I can see your 2022 Toyota RAV4 (rego 789XYZ) on the policy. I've got the date as this morning, Wednesday 28 October.

Can you tell me what happened, in your own words?

It was this morning, around 8ish. I was parked in the car park at work in Eagle Farm. When I came back out, there was a dent in the rear passenger door and a scratch down the side. Someone must have backed into me. Hmm, actually it was yesterday arvo, no wait, this morning. Sorry, I'm a bit flustered. Anyway, it's the rear passenger side. The car's still driving fine.

Thanks, Tom, that's clear. I've got it as this morning, Wednesday 28 October, around 8am, with a dent in the rear passenger door and a scratch down the side, while the car was parked at work in Eagle Farm.

What's the street address of the car park at your work?

I'm not sure of the exact street number, sorry. It's the car park behind the main office on Kingsford Smith Drive, I think? My work is one of those warehouse places near the Eagle Farm racecourse. I can look up the number if you need it.

That's enough to go on, no need to look up the number. I'll record it as the car park behind the main office on Kingsford Smith Drive, near the Eagle Farm racecourse.

Was around 8am when you parked the car, or when you came back and found the damage?

I came back out and found it. I'd parked there around 7:30 and went inside, so I'm not sure exactly when it happened, but it was between when I parked and when I came back out, which was about 8. I didn't see anyone hit it.

Thanks. So it happened between about 7:30am, when you parked, and about 8am, when you came back and found the damage, and you didn't see who did it.

Did you report it to the police, or did anyone leave a note or contact details on the car?
No police report yet, I didn't think to call them. There wasn't a note on the car or anything. I didn't see anyone around the car either. Should I report it to the police? I don't know if I need to.

I can't tell you whether you need to report it, because the rules can vary. I've noted your question on the claim so the claims consultant can talk it through with you.

Here's your claim as I have it:

- **Car (rego):** 789XYZ
- **Type of incident:** Hit while parked
- **When:** Wednesday 28 October 2026, between about 7:30am (when you parked) and about 8am (when you found the damage)
- **Where:** Car park behind the main office at your work, Kingsford Smith Drive, Eagle Farm, near the Eagle Farm racecourse (no street number)
- **What happened:** You parked at work around 7:30am and went inside. When you came back out about 8am there was a dent in the rear passenger door and a scratch down the side. You think someone must have backed into you. You didn't see it happen or anyone near the car, and no note was left.
- **Can be driven safely:** Yes
- **Who was driving:** Tom Nguyen (you parked the car)
- **Other party:** Unknown
- **Police reference:** Not reported to police yet

Is all of that correct?
